description: AI-powered lunar landing site tool for CLPS. Combines real-time NASA DONKI space weather with ARTEMIS, an IIT-based autonomous decision engine, to evaluate south pole sites: Sun/Earth position, power, comm windows, radiation risk. Built on ORBITAL_GUARDIAN satellite platform + Zenodo-published research.
summary:
Missions to the Moon's south pole face extreme lighting and communication constraints. Existing ephemeris tools are powerful but hard to use. The ARTEMIS Lunar Mission Browser turns that complexity into a traffic-light answer: pick candidate sites, pick dates, and instantly see when the Sun is up (power), when Earth is up (direct-to-Earth comm), and when both align -- "golden windows".

Built on JPL DE421 ephemerides and the IAU lunar rotation model, the tool evaluates Artemis III / CLPS candidate regions across any mission window: illumination %, Earth visibility % (with real libration), worst-case eclipse and blackout durations, and a composite site score. A polar sky view draws Sun and Earth tracks against the real LOLA terrain silhouette -- measured topography, not a flat horizon -- so planners see exactly which ridge blocks the link.

Engineering realism adds battery/array sizing for eclipse survival, slope hazard, distance to permanently shadowed regions (water ice), and DSN throughput in GB/day. Replay the IM-2 Athena window and the tool reproduces the failure mode that killed the mission -- ~24% illumination and ~10.6 days of continuous eclipse at Mons Mouton. Runs entirely on the user's machine -- no external services required. An optional ARTEMIS module (IIT-based) issues an autonomous LAND/RETURN verdict per site.
details:
THE PROBLEM

Planning CLPS deliveries to the lunar south pole requires coordinating science and engineering constraints: solar power depends on near-horizontal Sun geometry, and direct-to-Earth links depend on Earth staying above the horizon. Existing tools (SPICE, Horizons) require expert knowledge.

OUR SOLUTION

A web application where a mission planner, educator, or student can:

1. Select candidate landing sites (14 Artemis III / CLPS candidate regions preloaded).

2. Choose a mission window — or two windows to compare dates side-by-side.

3. Read the answer in plain language: GOOD / MARGINAL / POOR per site.

KEY FEATURES

- Elevation vs. horizon charts — Sun (power) and Earth (comm) elevation over the full window, with golden-window markers.

- Polar sky view with real terrain — Sun/Earth tracks drawn against the actual LOLA DEM ridge silhouette; tracks vanish behind terrain exactly where comm/power would be lost.

- Site comparison table — illumination %, Earth visibility %, golden %, longest eclipse, longest blackout, longest continuous sunlit, composite score.

- Date comparator — evaluate two mission windows and see the score delta per site.

- Engineering realism stack — battery + solar array sizing vs. worst eclipse (survival mode: continuous/battery/hibernation/RHU), slope hazard within landing radius, distance to nearest permanently shadowed region (ice/ISRU), DSN 34 m throughput (X/Ka band), surface temperature, and orbiter-relay fallback.

- Ask ARTEMIS — optional IIT Phi-inspired autonomous decision module issues a LAND/RETURN verdict with confidence, rationale, and a tamper-evident SHA-256 custody chain (custody_manifest.jsonl).

- Fully standalone — local DE421 ephemeris + IAU rotation; no internet or external service needed after first ephemeris download.

TECHNICAL APPROACH

- Ephemeris: JPL DE421 via Skyfield; Moon body-fixed frame built from the instantaneous Earth direction + IAU pole — captures libration in Earth visibility.

- Terrain masking: NASA LOLA 5 m/pix DEMs (south polar stereographic) ray-cast to a real 360° horizon profile; illumination/comm re-masked against the ridge.

- Engineering models: eclipse to battery/array sizing, LOLA slope statistics, PSR detection (horizon > max Sun elevation in all azimuths), free-space link budget to DSN 34 m BWG, radiative surface temperature, orbiter relay throughput.

- Backend: Python/FastAPI REST API; frontend: single-page HTML + Chart.js + canvas sky view.

- ARTEMIS: optional IIT 3.0-inspired Phi network integration metric + Sanchez-Copilot C_AI equation (calibrated against 476 IBM Quantum hardware runs on ibm_fez / ibm_torino) producing a LAND/RETURN verdict, logged to an append-only SHA-256 hash chain for flight-recorder auditability (graceful degradation when offline).

DATA & RESOURCES

- JPL DE421 ephemeris (NAIF)

- NASA LOLA 5 m/pix DEMs — south polar stereographic (PGDA, Sites 01/04/07/11/20/23 — every south-pole site published)

- IAU lunar rotation constants (libration in Earth visibility)

- DSN 34 m BWG link model (JPL 810-005 parameters)

- Artemis III / CLPS candidate landing regions (NASA announcements)

- Optional: NASA DONKI space weather (via contractor), NASA DSN Now

PRIOR WORK DISCLOSURE

The browser UI, CLPS evaluator, and contractor API were built for this challenge on top of our pre-existing open-source engines: ORBITAL_GUARDIAN (lunar/DSN tracking), ARTEMIS (IIT autonomy core), and Predictor_anomalo (space weather). All prior work is our own and disclosed per Space Apps rules.
